gallery.artist: Ken Lund from Reno, Nevada, USA
gallery.credit: The California State Normal School Bell, San Jose State University, San Jose, California
gallery.source: The California State Normal School Bell, San Jose State University, San Jose, California (3124843887)
gallery.description:
San Jose State University (often abbreviated San Jose State or SJSU) is a public university located in San Jose, California, United States. It is the founding school of the 23 campus California State University (CSU) system, and holds the distinction of being the oldest public institution of higher education on the West Coast of the United States.
Located in downtown San Jose, the SJSU main campus is situated on 154 acres (62 ha), or roughly 19 square blocks. SJSU offers 134 bachelor's and master's degrees with 110 concentrations. The university offers three joint doctoral degree programs, and will launch its first independent doctoral program in 2013. SJSU's total enrollment was 30,448 in 2012, including over 4,700 graduate students, the largest graduate student enrollment of any campus in the CSU system.
SJSU's student population is one of the most ethnically diverse in the nation, with large Asian and Hispanic enrollments, as well as the highest foreign student enrollment of all master's institutions in the United States.
Popular undergraduate majors at SJSU include business, engineering, visual and performing arts, nursing, psychology, justice studies, biology, kinesiology, journalism and computer science. Popular fields of study among graduate students include engineering, library and information science, education and social work.
San Jose State University claims to provide Silicon Valley firms with more engineering, computer science and business graduates than any other college or university, and philanthropic support of SJSU is among the highest in the CSU system.
SJSU sports teams are known as the Spartans, and compete in the Mountain West Conference (MWC) in NCAA Division I.
In 1881, a large bell was forged to commemorate the school. The bell was inscribed with the words "California State Normal School, A.D. 1881," and would sound on special occasions until 1946 when the college obtained new chimes.

gallery.filename: Cesar-chavez-arch.jpg
gallery.title: File:Cesar-chavez-arch.jpg
gallery.description:
This monument in commemoration of the life of Cesar Chavez lives on the campus of San Jose State University in downtown San Jose, California. The arch is capped by an eagle, the symbol of the United Farm Workers, and includes mosaic murals of Cesar Chavez and Dolores Huerta to celebrate their victories for California farm workers with 
a Mahatma Gandhi, Chavez' inspiration, mosaic as well. The circular mosaic path is treated with colors derived from the four Maya pre-Hispanic Codices discovered to date: Dresden, Paris, Madrid and Grolier. The arch stands in the middle of the passageway, representing the students going from having a vision to becoming an activist.

gallery.filename: San Jose State Aviation Department... just a bit before it disappeared (5721539342) (2).jpg
gallery.title: File:San Jose State Aviation Department... just a bit before it disappeared (5721539342) (2).jpg
gallery.description:
This is the 727-100 my beloved brother and I sat on the wing of and ate lunch and took pictures of SJC landings and takeoffs. I took this while the American MD-80 I was riding landed.  Not too long after I'm told the 727 was reduced to scrap on-site (I could have saved some of the instruments??) and the building and its contents are all gone now. Another chapter ends. I expect the big dumpsters were part of that effort. And, now that I think about it, I bed the CDF O2 spotter here is the one that wound up in pieces at the North Field at Oakland Airport.
Although engineless at this point, I still consider the 727 to qualifiy as a "trijet"
